propositions: fsck lacks detection of dirty-tree class wedges (tracked deletions, orphaned compaction leftovers, .tmp-event-* files, stale locks) that caused recent P0 outages
doctor --repair must heal the wedge non-destructively under properly-scoped write-lock windows, using two separate lock acquisitions because the write-lock is non-reentrant

fsck must classify and report three tracker-dirty kinds in both text and JSON output, with per-class counts and paths; doctor must extend its scan/repair registry to restore tracked deletions, quarantine regenerable leftovers, and leave .tmp-event-* for manual triage

doctor --repair must record a backup ref before mutating, run file mutations (checkout + quarantine-move) under one scoped write-lock, release that lock, then invoke reconverge in a second lock window to converge the store
the repair process must be idempotent (clean stores make zero changes and no backup ref) and preserve all file bytes via moves to quarantine, never deletions
